attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm 'won't' gives a scored forecast. The antecedent (OpenAI leaving the three providers in the lurch) is kept. 'Walks away from commitments' is a fair paraphrase of 'leaves in the lurch'.

contract.note: The plain reading (stranded capacity, no replacement customer) is ordinary for the absolute 'won't be anyone else'. It is strict but faithful. Setting no deadline is correct.

evidence.note: Cerebras company release dated 2026-10-27 about an inference partnership with Oracle. It does not show OpenAI abandoning capacity or anyone replacing it, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: No admissible evidence shows that OpenAI abandoned its commitments at CoreWeave, Cerebras or Oracle, so the antecedent is unknown and the conditional cannot be scored. No deadline was stated. The Cerebras–Oracle release is only context. A possible NVIDIA capacity arrangement could not be read and was not admitted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, as part of his argument about what follows OpenAI's death.

semantics.note: Firm 'will... find themselves unable' gives a scored forecast. The surrounding passage makes OpenAI's death the antecedent, and the normalisation keeps it.

contract.note: Reading 'unable to secure funding' as inability to raise new external debt or equity is the plain, ordinary sense. Setting no observation window is correct.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure dated 2026-10-28 shows it still operating, so the antecedent is not met. It says nothing about neocloud funding, so it is context, not contradiction.

reviews.rationale: The forecast only applies after OpenAI dies. The evidence shows OpenAI still operating at the cutoff, so the antecedent has not occurred and no financing outcome can be tested. No deadline was stated, so this is unresolved rather than contradicted.
